story.head: Nichushkin meets his old team
paras: The Blue Jackets (5-7-0) lost 3-1 to Dallas on Saturday, while the Avalanche have won three straight. Going in, the Avs are second in the Central (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Blue Jackets last in the Metropolitan (tied for 29th).

The Avalanche’s record (.633) is about what their chances are worth. The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.417) says: their chances are worth about .482, and their finishing has held them back.
This season, the Blue Jackets have been outscored 39-28, but only 22-18 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 11-4.

The Avalanche (2nd) and the Blue Jackets (3rd) both get their defensemen shooting. The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest) and play the league’s fastest games (1st). Colorado has scored 4.27 goals a game, the most in the league. As for the Blue Jackets, they keep things calm after the whistle (5th lowest). They also have a leaky penalty kill (30th), so the Avalanche kill penalties well, but them don’t. Columbus has scored 2.33 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league.

Nathan MacKinnon (9 G / 16 A / 25 P in 15 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is tied for fourth in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. Artturi Lehkonen (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for second in the NHL. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (7 G / 5 A / 12 P in 12 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Zach Werenski (0 G / 10 A / 10 P in 12 GP) isn’t far behind.
Mackenzie Blackwood (8-3-0 / .899 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to start for Colorado, and Cam Talbot (3-2-0 / .893 SV% in 5 GS) for Columbus.

At home, Rick Bowness likes to send Knies, Coyle and Olivier out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Lehkonen, MacKinnon and Nečas. Elsewhere, the Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Blue Jackets do.
